source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Record the appliance ID and type.
3. Note the date and time of the safety check.
4. List the safety check procedures performed, for example, insulation resistance testing, earth continuity check, polarity testing, power cord inspection, and functionality tests.
5. Document the failed test results clearly, specifying which test procedures were not met and the exact measurements taken.
6. Take photographs (if possible) of the faulty component, wire, plug, or any other part related to the failure. Ensure photos are clear and correctly labeled.
7. Record any visible damages, signs of overheating, or wear that may have contributed to the failure.
8. Include a short narrative explaining the context of the failure, such as unusual noises, sparks, smells, or physical malfunctions observed during the test.
9. Note any warnings or dangers associated with using the appliance in its present state, such as fire hazards or electric shock risks.
10. Recommend immediate repair, disposal
